facts.evidence: **Revenues** totaled **$31.6 billion**, up **2.3%** year-over-year (YoY), driven by **Advanced Connectivity** growth.
**Advanced Connectivity** revenues grew **5.1%** YoY to **$23.5 billion**
**Full-year 2026 guidance** remains unchanged, with **adjusted EBITDA*** growth of **3%–4%** and **adjusted EPS*** of **$2.25–$2.35**.

**$45 billion+** in shareholder returns (dividends + repurchases) planned for **2026–2028**, including **$10 billion in repurchases in 2026**. / **Capital allocation**: Accelerated share repurchases (**$10 billion in 2026**)
**Free cash flow*** was **$4.7 billion**, up from **$4.4 billion** YoY.
**Legacy segment** revenues declined **25.9%** YoY to **$1.6 billion**, reflecting continued copper network decommissioning.
**Net adds** totaled **1.0 million Advanced Connectivity customers**, including **367,000 fiber** and **279,000 fixed wireless** subscribers.

claims.claim: Second-quarter revenues totaled $31.6 billion.
Revenues were up 2.3% year over year.
Revenue growth was driven by Advanced Connectivity growth.
Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) was $0.65.
Year-ago adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) was $0.54.
Diluted EPS was $0.66.
Year-ago diluted EPS was $0.62.
Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $12.3 billion.
Adjusted EBITDA was up 5.2% year over year.
Operating income was $7.0 billion.
Year-ago operating income was $6.5 billion.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $4.7 billion in the quarter.
Year-ago free cash flow was $4.4 billion.
Capital expenditures were $5.7 billion.
Capital investment (non-GAAP) was $6.1 billion.
Advanced Connectivity revenues grew 5.1% year over year to $23.5 billion.
claims.note: The $23.5 billion / +5.1% figures are Advanced Connectivity SERVICE revenue. Total segment operating revenues were $28,615 million, up 4.1%. The brief presents a service-revenue line as the segment's revenues.

claims.claim: Advanced Home Internet revenue was $2.9 billion.
Advanced Home Internet revenue was up 27.3% year over year.
Net adds totaled 1.0 million Advanced Connectivity customers.
Fiber net adds were 367,000.
Fixed wireless net adds were 279,000.
Legacy segment revenues declined 25.9% year over year to $1.6 billion.
The Legacy revenue decline reflects continued copper network decommissioning.
Latin America revenues rose 16.1% year over year to $1.2 billion.
Latin America growth was driven by foreign exchange and wireless subscriber growth.
Full-year 2026 guidance remains unchanged.
2026 adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) growth is guided to 3%-4%.
2026 adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) is guided to $2.25-$2.35.
Capital investment (non-GAAP) is expected at $23-$24 billion annually through 2028.
AT&T plans $45 billion+ in shareholder returns (dividends plus repurchases) for 2026-2028.
That plan includes $10 billion in share repurchases in 2026.
Net debt (non-GAAP) was $126.4 billion at June 30, 2026.
$4.1 billion was returned to shareholders in the second quarter.
Second-quarter returns included $2.2 billion in common share repurchases.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) of $18 billion+ is projected for 2026.
Legacy segment EBITDA (non-GAAP) is expected to turn negative after 2027.
Legacy EBITDA turns negative as copper network costs decline.
claims.note: Inverts the release's explanation: Legacy EBITDA is expected to be negative UNTIL AT&T has substantially eliminated the direct costs of operating the copper network. The release does not attribute the negative EBITDA to declining copper costs.

claims.claim: Timing of the copper decommissioning depends on regulatory approvals.
AT&T remains on track to reach 40 million total fiber locations by the end of 2026.
AT&T remains on track to reach 60 million total fiber locations by the end of 2030.
